_comment: Native SQL for the per-form submission tables. Each published form has its own table in the FE schema, named on first publish (FE.SUB_<code>). {table} is the schema-qualified, bracket-quoted table and {name} its bare name for index and constraint names; both are checked against the SUB_[A-Z0-9_]+ alphabet by the store before they reach here. {column} is a validated data name wrapped in []. @named parameters carry every value. Edit here without redeploying (the file is reloaded on change).
TableExists: SELECT CASE WHEN OBJECT_ID(@tableName, N'U') IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END;
_comment_CreateTable: The schema guard lets a table be created before the first EF migration has run. Id defaults to NEWSEQUENTIALID so the clustered key stays in order; inserts read the value back with OUTPUT. There is no FormDefinitionId column: the table is the form.
CreateTable: IF SCHEMA_ID(N'FE') IS NULL EXEC(N'CREATE SCHEMA [FE]'); CREATE TABLE {table} ([Id] UNIQUEIDENTIFIER NOT NULL CONSTRAINT [DF_{name}_Id] DEFAULT NEWSEQUENTIALID() CONSTRAINT [PK_{name}] PRIMARY KEY, [VersionNo] INT NOT NULL, [Status] NVARCHAR(50) NULL, [ContextType] NVARCHAR(100) NULL, [ContextId] NVARCHAR(100) NULL, [SubmittedBy] NVARCHAR(256) NULL, [SubmittedByName] NVARCHAR(256) NULL, [SubmittedDate] DATETIMEOFFSET NULL, [ClientSubmissionId] UNIQUEIDENTIFIER NULL, [Created] DATETIMEOFFSET NOT NULL CONSTRAINT [DF_{name}_Created] DEFAULT SYSDATETIMEOFFSET());
ColumnNames: SELECT [name] FROM sys.columns WHERE [object_id] = OBJECT_ID(@tableName, N'U');
_comment_ColumnMaxLength: Bytes, not characters — an NVARCHAR(100) column reports 200. NVARCHAR(MAX) reports -1. Used to tell a column that is narrower than the type its field now wants.
ColumnMaxLength: SELECT [max_length] FROM sys.columns WHERE [object_id] = OBJECT_ID(@tableName, N'U') AND [name] = @columnName;
_comment_ColumnDecimalPrecision: Precision and scale of a DECIMAL column; no row when the column is not DECIMAL.
ColumnDecimalPrecision: SELECT [precision], [scale] FROM sys.columns WHERE [object_id] = OBJECT_ID(@tableName, N'U') AND [name] = @columnName AND [system_type_id] = TYPE_ID(N'decimal');
_comment_AlterColumn: Only ever issued to WIDEN an NVARCHAR or DECIMAL column — widening preserves every existing row, narrowing would fail or truncate.
IndexNames: SELECT [name] FROM sys.indexes WHERE [object_id] = OBJECT_ID(@tableName, N'U') AND [name] IS NOT NULL;
CreateSubmittedDateIndex: CREATE NONCLUSTERED INDEX [IX_{name}_SubmittedDate] ON {table} ([SubmittedDate] DESC) INCLUDE ([VersionNo], [ContextType], [ContextId]);
_comment_ContextIndex: Filtered to the rows that belong to something — a task, say — so a stand-alone fill costs nothing here. A filtered index needs QUOTED_IDENTIFIER and ANSI_NULLS ON; SqlClient sets both, but they are set explicitly because this can run on the submit path.
CreateContextIndex: SET QUOTED_IDENTIFIER ON; SET ANSI_NULLS ON; CREATE NONCLUSTERED INDEX [IX_{name}_Context] ON {table} ([ContextType], [ContextId]) INCLUDE ([VersionNo], [SubmittedDate]) WHERE [ContextType] IS NOT NULL;
_comment_ClientSubmissionIndex: Filtered so the rows that carry no client key are exempt from the uniqueness rule rather than colliding on NULL. This is what makes a retried submit idempotent.
CreateClientSubmissionIndex: SET QUOTED_IDENTIFIER ON; SET ANSI_NULLS ON; CREATE UNIQUE NONCLUSTERED INDEX [UX_{name}_ClientSubmissionId] ON {table} ([ClientSubmissionId]) WHERE [ClientSubmissionId] IS NOT NULL;
_comment_AcquireLock: Serialises changes to submission storage — one form's table, or the handing out of table names. Held until the surrounding transaction ends; a negative result means the wait timed out.
AcquireLock: DECLARE @result INT; EXEC @result = sp_getapplock @Resource = @resource, @LockMode = N'Exclusive', @LockOwner = N'Transaction', @LockTimeout = 30000; SELECT @result;
GetLatestByContext: SELECT TOP 1 {select} FROM {table} WHERE [ContextType] = @contextType AND [ContextId] = @contextId ORDER BY [SubmittedDate] DESC, [Created] DESC;
List: SELECT {select} FROM {table} WHERE (@contextType IS NULL OR [ContextType] = @contextType) AND (@contextId IS NULL OR [ContextId] = @contextId) ORDER BY [SubmittedDate] DESC, [Created] DESC OFFSET @skip ROWS FETCH NEXT @take ROWS ONLY;
Count: SELECT COUNT(1) FROM {table} WHERE (@contextType IS NULL OR [ContextType] = @contextType) AND (@contextId IS NULL OR [ContextId] = @contextId);
